plan.title: Batch-confounded DE analysis with caveats
plan.analytical_narrative: The design has 6 treated vs 6 control samples where batch B1 = all controls and B2 = all treated, a perfect confound. No statistical method (including ComBat, RUV, SVA) can distinguish a batch effect from a treatment effect when the two are perfectly aliased — there is no residual within-batch variation in condition to estimate the treatment effect independent of batch. Any DE list produced will reflect the sum of true treatment effect and any technical/batch difference between B1 and B2 processing, and this cannot be decomposed with the given design alone. Rather than silently running a batch-corrected DESeq2 model that would launder this confound into a false sense of validity, this plan: (1) runs standard DESeq2 DE analysis on raw counts with condition as the only term (batch cannot be added as a covariate here since it is collinear with condition — the design matrix would be rank-deficient), (2) explicitly runs and reports diagnostics (PCA, sample-sample correlation, library size/composition checks) that characterize whether the treated-vs-control separation looks like a global batch shift (affecting many unrelated genes/pathways non-specifically) versus a more targeted, biologically coherent signal, (3) performs pathway enrichment on the resulting DE list to see if it converges on coherent, plausible treatment-related biology, and (4) produces a report that flags the confound prominently and states that findings are hypothesis-generating only, pending replication in a study where treatment and batch are not aliased. No step attempts spurious deconfounding — that would misrepresent an unresolvable design flaw as a solved problem.
